artifacts.summary: Implemented the plan's ruling: git-commit-scoped.sh now classifies, guards, and commits the git rm --cached untracking shape end-to-end, with a regression suite, documentation, and a verified redeploy.

completion_data.completion_summary: Added a V11/V12 classification-and-guarded-commit path to git-commit-scoped.sh so a `git rm -r --cached <dir>` untracking (content left on disk) commits cleanly in both gitignored and non-gitignored repos without relocating any file, corrected the V8 intent-snapshot false-positive this shape would otherwise trigger, added a six-case regression cluster with a FAILS-before/PASSES-after demonstration, documented the sanctioned recipe in git-staging-scope.md, and confirmed the REQUIRED OUTCOME end-to-end against the redeployed script.

memory_candidates.content: Pattern for adding a new committable shape to a scoped-commit wrapper (git-commit-scoped.sh) without weakening existing gates: (1) classify the new shape in the PRE-add loop, routing it into the commit-pathspec set but explicitly OUT of the add-pathspec set -- this is what stops `git add` from silently reverting/re-tracking content that must stay untracked; (2) before switching to a wider commit primitive (e.g. a bare `git commit` instead of a pathspec-scoped one) to express a shape the narrower form structurally cannot, add an index-equivalence guard comparing the whole staged-index diff against the same diff restricted to the declared pathspecs -- equal proceeds, unequal refuses, so the wider primitive can never commit outside the caller's declared scope; (3) audit every pre-existing snapshot/intent gate (e.g. a pre-commit hash snapshot used for a post-commit integrity check) for a false-positive against the NEW shape's correct terminal state, and correct it via an explicit membership test (e.g. `git ls-tree` resolving HEAD-tracked members) rather than a string-prefix heuristic.

To demonstrate a new regression suite's FAILS-before property without ever running a red suite against the live source store: capture the pre-fix file via `git show <pre-fix-sha>:path > scratch-copy`, temporarily `cp` the scratch copy over the real file, run the full suite (new cases should fail, pre-existing cases should still pass), then immediately `cp` the known-good fixed copy (saved beforehand) back over the real file and re-verify with a final full run. This proves the new cases actually exercise the defect without ever leaving the working tree red or requiring a git checkout/stash that could disrupt concurrent writers on a shared tree.
